title: Musa’s Weeping • Sidrat al-Muntaha • Whom He Saw • The Question of Seeing • Three Gifts • From Fifty to Five

blocks.1: In the sixth heaven, Musa (AS). Salam was given. He replied. He said, welcome, brother and prophet. Then when the Prophet {{1}} passed beyond him, Musa (AS) wept. Someone asked, why do you weep?
blocks.3: Then I reached Musa (AS). Jibril (AS) said, this is Musa (AS), give him salam. I gave salam, and he replied. Then he said, welcome, righteous brother and righteous prophet. When I passed beyond him, he wept. He was asked, why do you weep? He said, I weep because a young man was sent after me; from his ummah more people will enter Paradise than from my ummah.{{1}}
blocks.4: This is not a weeping of envy. It is the weeping of a prophet. One who struggled with his people all his life, and now sees the followers of a prophet who came after him surpassing his own in number.{{1}}
blocks.6: In the seventh heaven, Ibrahim (AS). In the narration of Muslim, he is sitting with his back against a house.
blocks.8: In the seventh heaven I found Ibrahim (AS); he is leaning his back against al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur. Every day seventy thousand angels enter it; they never return to it.{{1}}
blocks.9: The name of that house is al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur. In the narration of Bukhari there is something more; that house was shown, and a tree.{{1}}
blocks.11: Al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur was raised before me. I asked Jibril (AS). He said, this is al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur; every day seventy thousand angels pray here. Those who go out once never return to it; that is their last turn. Then Sidrat al-Muntaha was raised before me. Its fruits were like the large jars of Hajar, its leaves like the ears of elephants. At its root are four rivers; two inner, two outer. I asked Jibril (AS). He said, the two inner are in Paradise; the two outer are the Nile and the Euphrates.{{1}}
blocks.12: Seventy thousand angels. A new group every day. Those who go out once never come back. Seventy thousand every day; then a fresh seventy thousand again. The rows of worship in the heavens never end.
blocks.13: Then Sidrat al-Muntaha. A lote tree; but what a tree! Fruits like big jars. Leaves like elephants’ ears. And at the root, four rivers. The Qur’an mentions this place in Surah an-Najm.{{1}}
blocks.15: 13. Indeed, he saw him (the angel) another time. 14. Near the Lote-Tree, whose name is Sidrat al-Muntaha. 15. Near it is the Garden of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma’wa). 16. When that which covered the Lote-Tree covered it. 17. The (Messenger’s) eye did not stray, nor did it exceed the limit. 18. The truth is, he saw some of the great signs of his Lord.{{1}}
blocks.16: What covered the tree? The Qur’an says, what was to cover it. And ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA) said, golden butterflies.{{1}}
blocks.17: About the beauty of the Sidrah the Prophet {{1}} himself said something.
blocks.19: Its leaves are like the ears of elephants, its fruits like large jars. When what was to cover it by Allah’s command covered it, it changed. No one of Allah’s creation can describe its beauty.{{1}}
blocks.20: No one can. Then one more scene.
blocks.22: Then I was taken up, until I came to a level ground where I heard the scratching of the pens.{{1}}
blocks.23: He was also made to enter Paradise.{{1}}
blocks.25: Then I was made to enter Paradise. In it were strings of pearls; and its soil was musk.{{1}}
blocks.27: The opening verses of Surah an-Najm show another side of this journey. The matter of seeing someone; twice.
blocks.29: 5. One taught him, a mighty one in power (the angel) 6. who has strength. So he appeared, 7. while he was on the highest horizon. 8. Then he came near and drew down. 9. Until he was at the distance of two bows, or even nearer. 10. Thus Allah revealed to His servant what He had to reveal.{{1}}
blocks.30: What is that true form like? ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA), explaining these verses, said that the Prophet {{1}} saw Jibril (AS), with six hundred wings.
blocks.32: (‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA)) told us that he (the Prophet {{1}}) saw Jibril (AS); he had six hundred wings.{{2}}
blocks.33: An angel of six hundred wings came to a man in human form; with revelation. And the second sighting was on this night of the Mi‘raj, near Sidrat al-Muntaha. Two places of two sightings; the horizon and the Sidrah.
blocks.35: In Surah an-Najm Allah said that the heart of the Prophet {{1}} did not err in what he saw. What did he see?
blocks.37: 11. His heart did not err in what he saw. 12. Will you then dispute with him about what he saw?{{1}}
blocks.38: The first answer of the verses is Jibril (AS); in his true form. The Prophet {{1}} first saw Jibril with the eye, then took him in with the heart. The heart did not err in it.{{2}}
blocks.39: A Tabi‘i went to ‘A’ishah (RA). Masruq. He asked, mother, did Muhammad {{1}} see his Lord?{{2}}
blocks.40: ‘A’ishah (RA) said, what you said made my hair stand on end.
blocks.42: Whoever tells you that Muhammad {{1}} saw his Lord has lied.{{2}}
blocks.43: She gave proof from the Qur’an. And she said, the one the Prophet {{1}} saw is Jibril (AS).
blocks.45: But he saw Jibril (AS) in his true form twice.{{1}}
blocks.46: On this question Salafi scholars hold to the words of ‘A’ishah and Abu Dharr (RA); seeing Allah with the eyes of this world is not established. Abu Dharr (RA) had asked the Prophet {{1}} directly.
blocks.48: I asked the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, did you see your Lord? He said, a light; how could I see Him?{{2}}
blocks.49: The words of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) have come, that he saw Him with the heart. Salafi scholars take this to mean seeing with the heart; not with the eye.
blocks.51: He saw Him with his heart.{{1}}
blocks.52: Ibn Taymiyyah said, there is no proof for seeing with the eye, and it is not even narrated from any of the Companions.{{1}}
blocks.54: At Sidrat al-Muntaha the Prophet {{1}} was given three things.
blocks.56: When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} was taken on the Isra’, he was brought to Sidrat al-Muntaha; it is in the sixth heaven. What rises up from the earth stops there; it is taken from there. What descends from above also stops there; it is taken from there. Allah said, ‘When that which covered the Lote-Tree covered it’ (Surah an-Najm 16). Ibn Mas‘ud (RA) said, golden butterflies. Then the Messenger of Allah {{2}} was given three things: the five daily prayers, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and, for any of his ummah who did not associate anything with Allah, forgiveness even of the ruinous major sins.{{3}}
blocks.57: One. Five daily prayers. Two. The last verses of Surah al-Baqarah. Three. Forgiveness of the major sins of an ummah who did not commit shirk. The second gift, in the Qur’an’s words, is this.
blocks.59: 285. The Messenger (that is, Hazrat Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace) believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and (so do) the believers (with him). All of them believe in Allah, in His angels, in His books and in His messengers. (They say,) We make no distinction between any of His messengers (that we would believe in some and not in others). And they say, we have heard (the commands of Allah and the Messenger attentively) and we are carrying them out gladly. Our Lord! We beg Your forgiveness, and to You is our return. 286. Allah does not burden anyone beyond their capacity. In their favour is what they do willingly, and against them is what they do willingly. (O Muslims! Make this du‘a to Allah:) Our Lord! Do not hold us to account if we make a mistake or slip. Our Lord! Do not place on us a burden like the one You placed on those before us. Our Lord! Do not load on us what we have no strength to bear. Pardon our faults, forgive us and have mercy on us. You are our Protector and Helper. So help us against the disbelieving people.{{1}}
blocks.60: The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him. The believers too. And they say, we heard and we obeyed. Allah does not burden anyone beyond their capacity. With these verses Surah al-Baqarah ends. In the hadith these very verses are what is called the gift of that night.{{1}}
blocks.61: The third matter is the reward of tawhid. The member of the ummah who, keeping away from shirk, will stand before Allah has a promise of forgiveness even for their ruinous sins.
blocks.63: Now comes the scene for which today’s dars carries its question. Allah made fifty prayers obligatory on the ummah. On the way down, the Prophet {{1}} came to Musa (AS) in the sixth heaven. Musa (AS) asked, what was commanded? Fifty prayers.
blocks.65: Your ummah will not be able to bear fifty prayers. By Allah, I tested people before you, and I tried my utmost with Bani Isra’il. Go back to your Lord.{{1}}
blocks.66: Musa (AS) speaks from his own experience. He had tried his utmost to manage Bani Isra’il. The Prophet {{1}} went back. Allah reduced it. Again he came to Musa (AS). Again the same words. Again going back. Again the reduction.{{2}}
blocks.67: At the end Musa (AS) said again, go back.
blocks.69: I have asked my Lord so much that I have become ashamed. Now I am content, and I submit.{{1}}
blocks.70: Then a call came from above.
blocks.72: Then the call was made: I have put My obligation into effect, I have lightened it for My servants, and I reward a good deed tenfold.{{1}}
blocks.73: And in another narration of Sahih al-Bukhari the matter is even clearer.
blocks.75: I went to Him again. He said, they are five, and they are fifty; the word is not changed with Me. I returned to Musa (AS), and he said, go again to your Lord. I said, I am ashamed before my Lord.{{1}}
blocks.76: In the narration of Sahih Muslim the calculation is stated directly.
blocks.78: O Muhammad, these are five prayers every day and night; ten for each prayer. So that is fifty. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, one good deed is written for them; if they do it, ten are written. Whoever intends an evil deed and does not do it, nothing is written; if they do it, one evil is written.{{1}}
blocks.79: Five prayers; five in number, fifty in reward. What Allah Himself made easy, we often find heavy even that.

footnotes.0: Sahih al-Bukhari 3887 (from Malik ibn Sa‘sa‘ah (RA)); Sahih al-Bukhari 3207
footnotes.1: Explanation of the weeping of Musa (AS): the words ‘not envy’ are this dars’s explanation; the hadith’s words are ‘I weep because…’ (Sahih al-Bukhari 3887). In the wording of Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 the word is ‘better than those who will enter Paradise from my ummah’ (أَفْضَلُ); in 3887, ‘أَكْثَرُ’ (more).
footnotes.3: Al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur, the Sidrah and the four rivers: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 and 3887. Variation in narrations about the location of Sidrat al-Muntaha: in this narration of Sahih al-Bukhari, after the seventh heaven; according to Sahih Muslim 173 (from ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA)), in the sixth heaven. Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, note 7 on Surah an-Najm 53:14–15 (p. 431): Sidrat al-Muntaha is a huge lote tree (jujube) of the upper world, near which Paradise is situated.
footnotes.5: Explanation of Surah an-Najm 53:13–18: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, note 7 (p. 431): this is the second occasion of seeing Jibril (AS) in his true form, which took place on the journey of the Mi‘raj. Note 8 (p. 432): ‘what covered it’ is beyond description; it is known from hadith that countless angels had then gathered over that tree in the form of golden butterflies. Note 9: the eye was not deceived, nor did it exceed the limit that Allah had set.
footnotes.6: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, Surah an-Najm 53:13–18, pp. 431–432 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.7: Golden butterflies: Sahih Muslim 173 (from ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA)): ‘قَالَ فَرَاشٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ’ ‘(what covered the tree was) golden butterflies’.
footnotes.9: Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (from Ibn ‘Abbas and Abu Habbah al-Ansari (RA); via Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri)
footnotes.10: Description of Paradise: the word in Sahih al-Bukhari 349 is ‘حَبَايِلُ اللُّؤْلُؤِ’ (strings of pearls); in some narrations ‘جَنَابِذُ اللُّؤْلُؤِ’ (domes of pearl) has come. Here the word of Sahih al-Bukhari 349 has been kept.
footnotes.12: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, Surah an-Najm 53:5–10, pp. 430–431 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.14: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, Surah an-Najm 53:11–12, p. 431 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.15: Explanation of 53:11: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, note 6 (p. 431): that is, it was not that the heart erred in understanding what the eye actually saw; note 7: the second occasion of seeing Jibril (AS) in his true form. Mufti Muhammad Shafi‘, Ma‘ariful Qur’an, Surah an-Najm 53:11: two explanations of these verses are mentioned; one is seeing Jibril in his true form (‘A’ishah, Ibn Mas‘ud, Abu Hurayrah and Abu Dharr (RA)), the other is seeing Allah (Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); Ma‘ariful Qur’an gives preference to the first view, because the basic meaning of the verb ‘ra’a’ is seeing with the eye and there is no need to take it in a figurative sense.
footnotes.16: Masruq and ‘A’ishah (RA): Sahih al-Bukhari 4855 (from Masruq): ‘I said to ‘A’ishah (RA), mother, did Muhammad {{1}} see his Lord? She said, what you said made my hair stand on end…’. Similar in Sahih Muslim 177.
footnotes.17: Sahih al-Bukhari 4855 (from Masruq, the statement of ‘A’ishah (RA))
footnotes.21: Salafi position: Islam Q&A (fatwa no. 12423): the narration of ‘A’ishah and Abu Dharr (RA) (Sahih al-Bukhari 4855; Sahih Muslim 178); taking Ibn ‘Abbas’s ‘he saw twice’ in the sense of ‘with the heart’; Ibn Taymiyyah: ‘There is no proof for seeing with the eye, and it is not narrated from any of the Companions’; al-Darimi (via Ibn al-Qayyim): ‘the consensus of the Companions that on the night of the Mi‘raj he did not see his Lord’. This is cited as the view of Salafi scholars.
footnotes.23: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:285–286, pp. 166–167 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.24: The third gift: Sahih Muslim 173: ‘وَغُفِرَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ أُمَّتِهِ شَيْئًا الْمُقْحِمَاتُ’ (for the member of the ummah who did not associate anything with Allah, the ‘muqhimat’, that is, the major sins that cast one into destruction, are forgiven). Scholars have explanations about the meaning of ‘muqhimat’ and its limits; here it is stated according to the hadith’s word.
footnotes.26: Steps of reduction: according to Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 and 3887, it was reduced by ten each time, finally five. According to Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (from Abu Dharr (RA)), each time by half (‘فَوَضَعَ شَطْرَهَا’), finally five. According to Sahih Muslim 162 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)), each time by five prayers (فَحَطَّ عَنِّي خَمْسًا). The accounts of the steps in the three narrations differ; the final result is one: five prayers.

o: Because fifty prayers had been made obligatory on his ummah, and they would not be able to bear that burden
Because the Prophet ﷺ took milk and put away wine, and so the ummah would find the way
Because more people from the Prophet’s ﷺ ummah would enter Paradise than from his own ummah
Because he had to pray inside the grave, and so had grown tired

quiz.q: Why does the dars say the weeping of Musa (AS) is not a weeping of envy?
o: Because he struggled with his people all his life, and sees the followers of the prophet who came after him growing in number
Because he envied the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer, and that weeping also included the count of his ummah
Because he was tired from praying inside the grave
Because he wept thinking of the disobedience of Bani Isra’il
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3887; the words ‘not envy’ are the dars’s explanation.

quiz.q: In the narration of Ibn Mas‘ud (RA), what covered the Sidrah tree?
o: A colour whose name the Prophet ﷺ does not know
Rows of seventy thousand angels
Strings of pearls and soil of musk
Golden butterflies
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 173; the mention of colours is in Sahih al-Bukhari 349.

quiz.q: How many wings did Jibril (AS) have, in the narration of Ibn Mas‘ud (RA)?
o: Six hundred
Seventy thousand
Twenty-seven
Forty

quiz.q: According to Sahih Muslim 173, which are the three gifts of the Mi‘raj?
o: Five daily prayers, a vessel of milk, and forgiveness of the major sins of an ummah who stayed away from shirk
Five daily prayers, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and forgiveness of the major sins of an ummah free of shirk
Five daily prayers, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and the salam of the angels of al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur
The fruit of the Sidrah, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and forgiveness of the major sins of an ummah free of shirk

quiz.q: What did Allah say in the final call (Sahih al-Bukhari 3207)?
o: If he has said it, then he has spoken truly; I believe him in news even farther than this
I have preferred some prophets over others, and I gave Dawud the Zabur
I put My obligation into effect, I lightened it for My servants, I reward a good deed tenfold
Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred; he does not speak from his own desire
quiz.e: «أَمْضَيْتُ فَرِيضَتِي وَخَفَّفْتُ عَنْ عِبَادِي وَأَجْزِي الْحَسَنَةَ عَشْرًا».

quiz.q: According to Sahih Muslim 162, what is the calculation by which five prayers are called fifty?
o: Twenty-seven times for each prayer in congregation
Forty times for each prayer prayed on time
Equal to bathing five times a day for the five prayers
Tenfold for each prayer

quiz.q: Why did Musa (AS) tell the Prophet ﷺ to go back about the burden on the ummah?
o: Because the Prophet ﷺ had asked him to try to reduce it further
Because Jibril (AS) had told him to ask his Lord
Because hearing the scratching of the pens at the Sidrah, he understood that prayer could be reduced further
From his own hard experience of managing Bani Isra’il

quiz.q: What is the meaning of ‘these are five, and these are fifty’?
o: Five in number, fifty in reward
Fifty in number, five in reward
Five in number, twenty-seven times less
In five prayers, the salam of fifty prophets

quiz.q: Which calculation settles ‘five in number, fifty in reward’?
o: Twenty-seven times for each prayer in congregation, so one hundred and thirty-five for the five prayers
The prayer of seventy thousand angels each day, so the same number for the five prayers
Tenfold reward for each prayer, so the reward of fifty in the five prayers themselves
With each prayer the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, so fifty in five prayers, so the five prayers become equal to the reward of fifty prayers
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 162: «لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ عَشْرٌ فَذَلِكَ خَمْسُونَ».

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ go back to Allah again and again?
o: To ask for more time for himself, so that the Buraq could return and Musa (AS) kept saying the same thing again and again
Because Jibril (AS) had told him to go back, to please his Lord
Because the Quraysh were waiting, and he had to return before morning
Because Musa (AS) advised that the ummah could not bear fifty prayers, so for the sake of the ummah

quiz.q: Someone repeatedly delays prayer, saying ‘in a little while’. Which scene of the Mi‘raj is most useful to make them understand?
o: The scene of Adam (AS) laughing on his right and weeping on his left, where the matter of his children’s ends is told
The scene of colour spreading over the Sidrah, which happened by Allah’s command and which no one can describe
The scene of the Buraq placing its foot at the edge of its sight, which shows the speed of the white animal
The scene of fifty being reduced to five on Musa’s (AS) advice, with the reward remaining fifty
